levers.name: Ping wait
levers.why: The 90s to 60s cut in 4.2 is the strongest suspected cause: first pings missed went from 0.7% to 11.4%.

levers.name: Penalties and credit on the score
levers.why: Misses count like refusals today (-0.12 vs +0.08). This is what pushed the quiet four's scores to the floor.

levers.name: Score limits, starting score and recovery
levers.why: No recovery exists today; a responder at 0 needs seven taken pings to reach 0.5.

levers.name: Ranking weights and inputs
levers.why: Decides who is asked first, and so how much goes to out-of-area responders, who took 0 of 178 out-of-area pings before 4.2.

levers.name: Walking the list and retries
levers.why: Unfilled callouts rose from 5.1% to 10.8%, all from callouts ending on a miss; 35 of 40 stopped after one ping.

levers.name: Push, alert and answer handling
levers.why: The brief relies on a harder-to-miss alert to win back the 60s miss increase.

levers.name: Who is on the list
levers.why: Short lists are the likely cause of unfilled callouts; available_for is a stub here.

levers.name: Availability record read by Supply
levers.why: A contract with Rook Supply. Any change to its shape needs Supply told before it ships.

agreed_constants.name: OFFER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
agreed_constants.why: The brief keeps the 60s ping wait. Changing it also breaks measuring each release on its own.

agreed_constants.why: Changes who counts as close; not part of the brief.
